title: Add incremental-index RAG CLI and live-indexing notebook templates
author: Aisha Kaur
release_notes: Add new incremental-index CLI and three quickstart templates (py notebook, ts example, minimal CLI) to demonstrate safe live indexing for RAG workflows; added docs page and tutorial notebook. No breaking API changes.
description: Motivation: teams building RAG systems often need to iterate on indexes continuously as new documents arrive (changefeeds, user uploads, streaming sources). Existing quickstarts demonstrate one-off ingestion into a vector DB but lack a small, repeatable CLI and notebook workflow for incremental indexing, local testing, and schema drift debugging. This PR introduces a lightweight CLI tool, a set of incremental-index notebook templates (Python) and a complementary TypeScript example that integrates the CLI with a running agent for tool-calling and reindex-on-demand. The goal is to provide a minimal, production-adjacent pattern for: 1) running idempotent upserts into an index, 2) emitting compact diff telemetry for indexing jobs, and 3) safe rollbacks when embeddings or encoding pipelines change. What this PR contains: - lightweight CLI: tools/incremental_index_cli.py (Python), minimal flags for --source, --batch-size, --dry-run, --checkpoint-file, and --embed-model to make it easy to script in CI and notebooks - notebook templates: notebooks/incremental_index_playbook.ipynb (annotated tutorial for data scientists showing incremental runs, checkpoint inspection, and KV cache warmup) - TypeScript example: examples/ts-incremental-watcher/ that listens for file additions and hits the CLI using child_process and demonstrates tool-calling from an agent to trigger upstream reindex and patching metadata - docs page: docs/quickstarts/incremental-indexing.md with interactive steps, recommended runtimes, and observability knobs (how to expose token-level cost in console, suggested canary prompts) - tests and smoke harness: tests/integration/test_incremental_index.sh and a small fixture data set under examples/fixtures/ - README changes and local-run scripts for CI and dev loop Checklist: - [x] CLI implementation and argument parsing - [x] Notebook template with explanatory narrative - [x] TypeScript watcher example and README - [x] Docs page and quickstart sidebar link - [x] Basic integration smoke test - [x] Added Linear links and changelog blurb Notes on design decisions: - The CLI uses a compact checkpoint file (JSONL with last-processed id and cursor token) to keep the implementation filesystem-first and runnable in air-gapped installs (aligns with Redwood Private needs). - We intentionally avoid introducing a new DB dependency; the examples work with in-memory sqlite for the notebook and provide guidance for Milvus/Weaviate/Redis in the docs. - The TS watcher intentionally shells out to the CLI to show how teams can decouple the indexing control plane from the embedding workers (mirrors some production patterns). Related: ENG-1120 (batching improvements) and ENG-1299 (observability probes).
